open_points.subject: Function purity and admissibility
open_points.text: “A flow is a small proven graph of two kinds of node: a pure function an agent wrote” and “No effectful, stateful or network-capable function” conflict with “code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
open_points.question: Is an implementation that obtains time or randomness through a route the sandbox does not detect a valid function eligible for admission, or is it forbidden because function implementations must be pure?
options: It is eligible and may be admitted when its observed trial outputs pass.
It violates the function model and must be refused even if its observed outputs pass.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as eligible because the changed passage expressly says to judge it by its outputs.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty corpus whose case expects output 1, and an implementation obtains an undetected random bit and returns it.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The admission execution happens to return 1 on every case.
outcomes: The kernel admits and activates it because undetected time/chance dependencies are judged by their outputs.
The kernel refuses it because a random-dependent implementation is not a pure function and the product excludes stateful functions.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and anyone running the slot see whether the implementation becomes active.

open_points.subject: Determinism of AdmissionVerdict for undetected nondeterministic implementations
open_points.text: K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” while K-02 permits code that gets time or chance another way to go undetected and be “judged by its outputs like any other”; M08 now records the first verdict once and reuses it, never computing it again.
open_points.question: What does “deterministic verdict” mean when an admitted implementation may produce different results on repeated executions of the same corpus?
options: The first admission observations determine a permanent cached verdict for the implementation and corpus digest, even though another execution could yield the opposite verdict.
Admission must exclude or otherwise classify such an implementation so the verdict is determined by the implementation and corpus rather than by the first observed random or time-dependent result.
open_points.default_guess: Cache the verdict from the first admission observations, following the changed M08 rule literally.

witness.initial: A corpus has one case expecting true, and an implementation returns an undetected random boolean.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation when it returns true during admission.
The same implementation and unchanged corpus are submitted again at a time when executing it would return false.
outcomes: The original admitted verdict is reused and the implementation is activated again without execution.
A deterministic-admission reading cannot let the verdict depend permanently on the first random observation and therefore refuses or re-evaluates/classifies the implementation differently.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and subsequent flow runners see whether the implementation is active and runnable.
